extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (design, plant, and PCT applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph guidance from the MPEP covering design patent drawing/specification requirements, new-matter and amendment rules, copyright/trademark overlap, continuity/priority (CIP/foreign), plant patent disclosure rules, novelty/inventive-step/industrial-applicability (PCT), and unity-of-invention standards. Intended to be used by examiners preparing Office actions and by applicants to correct deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible Descriptive Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The descriptive statement included in the specification is impermissible because [1]. ... the description should be canceled as any description of the design in the specification, other than a brief description of the drawing, is generally not necessary, since as a general rule, the illustration in the drawing views is its own best description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1503.01, subsection II. Examiner Note: In bracket 1, insert the reason why the descriptive statement is improper. Recommendation: delete/cancel descriptive statements beyond a brief drawing description; specify why improper in Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic Feature Statement (permissible form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'characteristic features' statement describing a particular feature of novelty or nonobviousness in the claimed design may be permissible in the specification. Such a statement should be in terms such as 'The characteristic feature of the design resides in [1],' or if combined with one of the Figure descriptions, in terms such as 'the characteristic feature of which resides in [2].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May serve later to limit the claim (McGrady v. Aspenglas). Examiner Note: insert brief but accurate description of the feature of novelty or nonobviousness in brackets 1 and 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Statement Caution — overall appearance controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of a feature statement in the specification is noted. However, the patentability of the claimed design is not based on the specified feature but rather on a comparison of the overall appearance of the design with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Leslie. Do not treat a characteristic feature statement as determinative of design patentability; assess total/overall appearance against prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity for Good Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing constitutes the whole disclosure of the design; it must be so well executed in clarity and completeness that nothing regarding the design sought to be patented is left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient drawings may be fatal to validity (35 U.S.C. 112(a)) and may negatively affect effective filing date of continuations. Emphasize clear, complete drawings showing claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken Lines Not Permitted to Indicate 'Unimportant' Features
rubrics_metrics.description: The ornamental design which is being claimed must be shown in solid lines in the drawing. Broken lines for the purpose of indicating unimportant or immaterial features of the design are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no portions of a claimed design which are immaterial or unimportant. See In re Blum and In re Zahn. Examiner should require solid-line disclosure for claimed features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Broken Lines to Show Environmental Structure (allowed with limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental structure may be illustrated by broken lines in the drawing if clearly designated as environment in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.152 and MPEP § 1503.02 III. Examiner Note: Do not use form paragraph in international design applications. If used, include a statement describing the broken lines (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Description Statement for Broken Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement similar to: 'The broken line showing of [1] is for the purpose of illustrating [2] and forms no part of the claimed design.' should be inserted in the specification preceding the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert name of structure. In bracket 2 insert 'portions of the “article”' or 'environmental structure.' Do not use in international design applications. Ensure proper tense in bracket 3 ('must be' or 'has been').

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate Figure When Broken Lines Obscure Full-Line Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where superimposed broken lines showing environmental structure obscure the full line disclosure of the claimed design, a separate figure showing the broken lines must be included in the drawing in addition to the figures showing only claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids obscuring the claimed design and ensures clarity of what is claimed in solid lines (35 U.S.C.112(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken Line Boundary Statement (broken lines define bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following statement must be used to describe the broken line boundary of a design: 'The [1] broken line(s) define the bounds of the claimed design and form no part thereof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert type of broken line (e.g., dashed). Do not use in international design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for New Matter — 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (Design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) as failing to comply with the description requirement since the [1] introduces new matter not supported by the original disclosure. The original disclosure does not reasonably convey to a designer of ordinary skill that applicant was in possession of the design now claimed at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Daniels; In re Rasmussen. Specify in bracket 1 whether new drawing or amendment to drawing/title/spec. In bracket 2 specifically identify the new matter. Suggest ways to overcome (e.g., correct bracket in figures or delete descriptive statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to Disclosure Objected Under 35 U.S.C. 132 / 37 CFR 1.121 (New Matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The [1] is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 and 37 CFR 1.121 as introducing new matter not supported by the original disclosure. The original disclosure does not reasonably convey that applicant was in possession of the amended subject matter at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what was amended in bracket 1, identify lack of support in bracket 2, and suggest how to overcome in bracket 3 (e.g., omit broken-line environmental structure or amend title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright Notice Inclusion Conditions for Design Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the PTO to permit inclusion of a copyright notice in a Design Patent application under specified conditions: placement adjacent to copyright material; if on the drawing, limited print size (1/8" to 1/4") and placed within the 'sight' of the drawing immediately below the figure; content limited to legally required elements (e.g., '© 1983 John Doe'); a waiver statement must be included in the specification; post-Notice of Allowance inclusion only if 37 CFR 1.312 criteria met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion permitted only if waiver includes the exact language that the copyright owner has no objection to facsimile reproduction by anyone of the patent document as it appears in USPTO records. Any deviation may result in refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Material in Drawing — Specification Amendment Required
rubrics_metrics.description: If trademark material forms part of the claimed design, the specification must be amended to include a statement preceding the claim identifying the trademark material and the name of the owner of the trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: identify trademark material in bracket 1 and trademark owner in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Wording Requirements — 'As Shown' and 'As Shown and Described'
rubrics_metrics.description: For proper form (37 CFR 1.153 or 1.1025), claims should read: '[I/We] claim: The ornamental design for [article] as shown.' or '... as shown and described.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert 'must be' or 'has been' as appropriate; bracket 2 insert 'I' or 'We'; bracket 3 insert title of article. Use correct statutory/formal wording to avoid rejection under 35 U.S.C.112(b) or form rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of 'And Described' to Claim — When Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of [1] -- 'and described' -- [2] added to the claim after 'shown.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert reason in bracket 1 and proper tense in bracket 2. Use when the description adds necessary limiting disclosure to the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment May Not Be Possible — fatal defect/new matter risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim might be fatally defective; it might not be possible to [1] without introducing new matter (35 U.S.C. 132, 37 CFR 1.121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed differences are only minute variations, the test for design patentability is unobviousness in overall appearance, not small variations. Cite In re Frick and In re Lamb. If amendment would introduce new matter, advise that amendment may be impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (Single Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: It would have been obvious to a designer of ordinary skill not later than the effective filing date of the present claimed invention to [1] (or pre-AIA wording: 'at the time the invention was made to [1]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert explanation of the use of the reference in bracket 1. For design patents, explain how the primary reference teaches the claimed appearance and why it renders claims obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (Multiple References)
rubrics_metrics.description: This modification of the primary reference in light of the secondary reference is proper because the applied references are so related that the appearance of features shown in one would suggest the application of those features to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Rosen, Carter, Glavas; explain why a designer skilled in the art would combine elements. Provide reasoning how combination would be within ordinary skill (In re Antle, In re Nalbandian).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Indefinite Language ('or the like') by Examiner’s Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase [1] in the claim following the title renders the claim indefinite. By authorization of [2] in a telephone interview on [3], the phrase has been cancelled from the claim and at each occurrence throughout the papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert objectionable phrase (e.g., 'or the like'). Use Ex parte Pappas precedent. Note exemptions for oath/declaration per 35 U.S.C.112(b) and 37 CFR 1.153.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quayle Action (Ex parte Quayle) — Allowance Except Formal Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is in condition for allowance except for the following formal matters: [1]. Prosecution on the merits is closed in accordance with Ex parte Quayle. A shortened statutory period for reply is TWO MONTHS from mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert outstanding formal matters in bracket 1. Use when claims are allowable on merits but formal corrections remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected Drawing Sheets Required — consequence of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to submit replacement correction sheets overcoming all deficiencies in the drawing disclosure or an explanation why corrections/additional views are unnecessary will result in rejection of the claim under 35 U.S.C.112(a) and (b) being made FINAL in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt timely correction required to avoid final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-Part (CIP) Not Entitled to Benefit of Parent — Written Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to this design application as a continuation-in-part under 35 U.S.C.120 is acknowledged. Applicant is advised that the design claimed in the present application is not disclosed in the parent application; therefore the parent application does not satisfy the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C.112(a) under 35 U.S.C.120 and the present application is not entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because not entitled to earlier filing date, the parent application is available as prior art under 35 U.S.C.102. Use form paragraph accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIP Preface for Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(d)/172 — foreign priority effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parent application claimed foreign priority that matured into a patent/registration before the filing of the present application and was filed more than six months before the present filing, the foreign patent/registration qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(d)/172.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph followed by rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(d)/103(a) as appropriate; do not consider entitlement to priority unless needed to avoid intervening prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIP Caution — Claim to Foreign Priority, Status Unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is advised that the design disclosed in the parent application is not the same as in this application; parent claimed foreign priority. Applicant is requested to inform the Office of the status of the foreign application to which priority is claimed because the foreign patent/registration may qualify as prior art if matured and filed > 6 months before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request applicant to provide status of the foreign application; if foreign matured earlier, it may be prior art under pre-AIA provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisclosed Visible Surfaces/Portions Not Part of Claimed Design
rubrics_metrics.description: The [1] of the article [2] not shown in the drawing or described in the specification. It is understood that the appearance of any part of the article not shown in the drawing or described in the specification forms no part of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert surfaces in bracket 1 and 'is'/'are' in bracket 2. Cite In re Zahn. Determination of patentability is based on shown/described article only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of Allowability Withdrawn — reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of allowability set forth in the previous action is withdrawn and prosecution is reopened in view of the following new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the new ground(s) of rejection and resume prosecution; explains procedural posture change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Specification Must Particularly Point Out Asexual Reproduction Method (37 CFR 1.163(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is objected to because the specification does not 'particularly point out where and in what manner the variety of plant has been asexually reproduced.' Correction is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert specific deficiency in bracket. Provide full details of asexual reproduction method to satisfy rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Colors Specified Must Correspond to Those Shown
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure is objected to under 35 U.S.C.112(a) because the [1] colors specified fail to correspond with those shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify mismatch in bracket 1. Ensure color descriptions match color drawings/photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Rejection for Non-Support for Colors (35 U.S.C.112(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C.112(a) as being unsupported by a clear and complete disclosure with regard to [1] colors, for the following reasons: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify color-related deficiencies and reasons in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Name/Denomination of Variety Required (37 CFR 1.121(e), 1.163(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure objected to because no 'variety denomination' of the instant plant has been set forth; correction by adding such a name is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add variety denomination to disclosure to comply with rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Latin Name of Genus and Species Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure objected to because the Latin name of genus and species of the plant claimed has not been set forth. Correction by adding such a name is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add correct Latin binomial to the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Color Drawings Must Be Submitted in Duplicate (37 CFR 1.165(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure is objected to because applicant has not provided copies of the color drawing in duplicate. Correction is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit duplicate color drawings per rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent — Drawing Figures Must Be Competently Executed (37 CFR 1.165(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure is objected to because Fig. [1] is not artistically and/or competently executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify figure number in bracket 1 and require competent redrawing or correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 35 U.S.C.112 Rejection Form — 35 U.S.C.112 Rejection Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C.112 [1] because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to state specific statutory deficiency and reasoning in bracket 2; add detailed reasoning in bracket 3 as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Lacks Novelty (PCT Article 33(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] novelty under PCT Article 33(2) as being anticipated by [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and the reference(s) in brackets. Use when claim is anticipated by prior art; follow with reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Lacks Inventive Step / Obviousness (PCT Article 33(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] an inventive step under PCT Article 33(3) as being obvious over [2] (or over [2] in view of [3] for multiple references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and prior art references; explain rationale of combination and reasoning in bracket 4 as needed. If inventive step lacking, follow with appropriate PCT form paragraphs (18.02/18.02.01/18.02.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Industrial Applicability (PCT Article 33(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] industrial applicability as defined by PCT Article 33(4). [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims meet industrial applicability, use form paragraph 18.04.01 and potentially 18.04. If not, follow with 18.03 (Lacks Industrial Applicability). Insert explanation in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Unity of Invention Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. 'Special technical features' are those technical features that define a contribution which each of the claimed inventions makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine unity without regard to claim format. For multiple categories, unity present only for permitted combinations (product+manufacture process, product+use, product+process+use, process+apparatus, product+process+apparatus). Follow with lack-of-unity form paragraphs (18.06 etc.) when not met. Use PCT Rule 13.1/13.2 and 37 CFR 1.475.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Lack of Unity Grouping and Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: When lack of unity, list Groups (e.g., Group I, claims X–Y drawn to ...) to identify groups of claims/inventions that are not linked by a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 18.06–18.06.02 to identify groups, insert Roman numerals, claim numbers, and names of grouped inventions. If claims are to multiple products/processes/apparatuses, group appropriately and explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Reasons for Lack of Unity (no same or corresponding special technical features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of inventions do not relate to a single general inventive concept because they lack the same or corresponding special technical features for specified reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 18.07 and follow with 18.07.01–18.07.03. Explicitly identify which groups lack the shared feature and explain why it fails to be a 'special technical feature' that contributes over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Shared Technical Feature Lacks Contribution Over Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: [1] lack unity because even though the inventions require the technical feature of [2], this technical feature is not a special technical feature as it does not make a contribution over the prior art in view of [3]. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify groups in bracket 1, the shared feature in bracket 2, prior art references in bracket 3, and explain in bracket 4 how the feature lacks novelty or inventive step in view of those references.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Markush Group Alternatives of Chemical Compounds Not of Similar Nature (unity test for Markush)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single claim defines alternatives of a Markush group of chemical compounds, alternatives are of a similar nature if: (A) all alternatives have a common property or activity; AND (B)(1) a common structure is present (a significant structural element shared by all alternatives); OR (B)(2) if common structure cannot unify, all alternatives belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this two-part test to determine if Markush alternatives meet unity; if not, lack of unity applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT — Heading for Lack of Unity Action During International Phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin all Lack of Unity actions for PCT applications with the heading 'REQUIREMENT FOR UNITY OF INVENTION' and follow with applicable form paragraphs (18.06–18.07.03 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statutory/regulatory citations (37 CFR 1.475) and explain how groups fail unity under PCT Rule 13.1/13.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens Required (Plant Applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant [1] required to submit [2] in accordance with 37 CFR 1.166.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when physical specimens are required for plant applications; insert pluralization and items required in brackets.
